tagline: Sustainable cuminaldehyde from Pseudomonas putida, and NetFlux, a web tool that turns a genome-scale metabolic model into a drawable pathway and a ranked list of knockouts.
summary: MAHEK addresses the fragrance industry's dependence on petrochemical synthesis and wasteful seed extraction by producing cuminaldehyde biologically. The chassis is Pseudomonas putida F1, a solvent-tolerant soil bacterium that already makes cuminaldehyde as an intermediate in p-cymene degradation; CRISPR-Cas9-mediated homologous recombination knocks out cymC, the p-cumic aldehyde dehydrogenase, arresting the pathway exactly at the target compound. The dry lab's deliverable is NetFlux, a React + FastAPI web application that compresses a genome-scale metabolic model into a readable 'production corridor' using a novel extraction algorithm (SCOPE) and then pools OptKnock and OptForce into one co-ranked list of knockout and regulation strategies, each traced to the gene and linked to BiGG. The team also won the Inclusivity Award for work with visually impaired learners that ended in Vision Empower adopting their tactile models for use in schools across India.

dry.frameworks: React + TypeScript single-page frontend split into three modules (parameter panel, pathway map viewer, interventions table) sharing one run state; FastAPI backend with Pydantic request/response schemas, auto-generated OpenAPI 3.1 documentation and a Swagger UI at /docs; a JobManager running strain design on a bounded background worker pool so heavy requests do not time out; SQLite (mfghub.db) as the model/reaction/metabolite/gene/medium catalogue, rebuilt from the GEMs on every server image build; and Docker Compose bringing up database, API and web client together. Core science runs on COBRApy.
dry.dataviz: Pathways are drawn as interactive metabolic maps flowing strictly left to right, with line width proportional to mass flow, metabolites as nodes carrying compartment suffixes, reactions as arrows colour-coded by their FVA annotation, and the substrate-to-target corridor explicitly highlighted. Hovering a reaction opens an inspection card with reaction name and ID, knockout-candidate status, flux and FVA range, coupling and bounds, subsystem, gene associations and gene rules, and its producers and consumers. Each click of Generate opens its parameters in a new tab so settings can be compared side by side. Results export as GraphML, JSON and CSV straight from the browser. The interventions table shows a baseline header (wild-type growth rate, yield floor and ceiling) against which every ranked design is judged, and separates committed 'Ranked Designs' from weaker single-reaction 'Hypotheses (leads)', with the wiki telling users not to compare yield numbers across the two tables.
dry.datascience: Benchmarked without a ground truth by defining what a useful pathway must do and measuring that instead. SCOPE was run on 9 GEMs with up to 5 target products each, 40 organism-product pairs in total: 100% of extracted pathways were fully connected from substrate to target, and the mean corridor was 55.1 reactions against a mean model size of 934, i.e. 7.8% of the network (models up to 1,762 reactions reduced to about 55). Essential reactions were identified independently with FVA and then checked for recall: 20.3 essential reactions per product on average, 17.5 retained, overall recall 0.863, above 0.90 in five of nine organisms, with the weakest cases (iJN1463 at 0.616, iJN1026 at 0.719) reported rather than hidden. Eleven curated GEMs ship with the tool, covering bacteria, a cyanobacterium, an archaeon, yeast and a diatom. The metabolic model behind the wet lab extended iJN1463 with the full p-cymene degradation route (cymA, cymB, cymC, cmtA-cmtE), linking to native metabolism through OP4ENH.
dry.software: NetFlux solves two linked problems in metabolic engineering: genome-scale models are too large to read, and strain-design algorithms waste most of their compute on reactions that can never carry flux. Its five-stage pipeline is the substance. Stage 1 solves FBA then pFBA and converts the flux distribution into a Mass Flow Graph (nodes = reactions, edges = metabolite mass flow). Stage 2 applies FASTCC against a fixed consistency threshold to strip blocked reactions, which the team identifies as the single largest source of computational expense. Stage 3 is SCOPE, their GUDIE-derived extractor: log-normalise the heavy-tailed edge weights, compute a flux-coupling score per reaction against the target, seed an interest signal at the target and propagate it with Personalised PageRank, combine coupling and interest into a per-edge score, expand outward over a bounded number of hops admitting reactions above a threshold anchored to the target's immediate neighbourhood, then an optional repair step that closes a broken corridor with a flux-weighted shortest path. Stage 4 annotates the corridor with FVA so each reaction is typed as essential-and-fixed, flexible, or a natural up/downregulation candidate. Stage 5 pools OptForce and OptKnock and co-ranks their proposals into one ordered list, resolving each to a gene linked to BiGG. Two design decisions stand out for reuse: the REST API is versioned, OpenAPI 3.1-specified and language-agnostic with async job polling (submit, get a job_id, poll), and all compute is deliberately RAM-only, with uploaded models referenced by short-lived tokens, a 30-minute SessionCache, and nothing a client submits ever written to disk or database. Users can upload their own GEM as .json or .sbml. It is self-hosted rather than publicly deployed: 'git clone https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/mit-mahe/netflux && docker compose up --build', then http://localhost:5173/, with stated system requirements of 2-4 GB RAM, any modern multi-core CPU and no GPU. A video guide and a step-by-step interpretation guide are on the wiki, and the limitation is stated plainly: constraint-based predictions describe what the network allows at steady state, not kinetics or regulation, so every strategy is a wet-lab hypothesis. Repo: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/mit-mahe/netflux (team repo https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/mit-mahe).

good.publicEngagement: Sessions were run across India in English, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada and Marathi so language would not be a barrier, and deliberately extended beyond students: the team visited old age homes to learn how residents' associations with traditional scents had changed over their lifetimes, then introduced them to synthetic biology. Workshops included household-materials DNA extraction from bananas at Purple Space Library Manipal (50 students, grades 1-7, split by age group), recombinant DNA via insulin at GenWise Camp, and deeper project discussion with grade 11-12 biology students at Vidya Mandir Chennai. Teachers were walked through each protocol step so they could keep running the demonstration after the team left. 'Beyond Sight', an audio-only podcast, carried five conversations with visually impaired professionals (a radio jockey, a geneticist, the founder of assistive-technology company TorchIT, an ophthalmologist, and one of only three blind women to have submitted before the Supreme Court of India). A Colourblind Awareness Day Instagram series ran on 6 September.
good.ihp: Stakeholder analysis walked the whole cumin supply chain, from traders who buy directly from farmers to internationally working perfumers, finding that each group holds a different version of the same problem. Hard numbers anchor the premise: India supplies about 70-80% of world cumin, the 2026 crop was projected at 9.0-9.2 million bags against roughly 11 million in 2025 (a 15-20% decline), hydrodistillation yields about 2.56% essential oil, and cuminaldehyde is a fraction of that. The decisive conversation was with Givaudan, which revealed that fragrance houses procure whole cumin essential oil rather than isolated cuminaldehyde; this redirected the team's target customer from fragrance houses to aroma compound manufacturers, where demand for isolated, sustainably produced cuminaldehyde actually exists. The inclusivity work was itself integrated rather than decorative: conversations with Vision Empower (IIIT Bangalore) identified that Indian educational structures restrict visually impaired students from science, and the team then built tactile models, trialled them with Mrs Nagarathna, a visually impaired educator, revised on her feedback, and tested with a ninth-grade student. Fixes were deliberately minimal and buildable from cheap materials: the existing DNA model distinguished bases only by colour, so each base got a texture instead (adenine smooth tape, thymine jute, guanine bubble wrap, cytosine velvet) wrapped around the existing model so it did not need rebuilding; the mitosis model's components were only drawn on, so they were rebuilt in clay with pipe-cleaner chromosomes. Vision Empower approved both the content and the models and will use them across their associated schools. A separate conversation with an Indian Sign Language expert established that, unlike ASL, ISL has no centralised place to learn it, which the team records as a gap they did not close.
good.realWorld: A consumer survey found the barrier is information rather than opposition, with respondents already aware of land use, extraction and climate pressures and nearly half willing to pay slightly more for lower environmental impact, though more were worried about long-term effects of ingredients made by engineered microorganisms. Producer-side work found that Indian companies import aroma compounds from China, the UAE and France despite domestic cumin dominance, and that price is the deciding factor for buyers because raw material cost passes straight to consumers. The team wrote 'An iGEMer's Guide to Upscaling', a structured upscaling and biomanufacturing guide, after finding no iGEM-oriented resource bridging flask scale to industrial scale, and 'The Aroma Atlas', a catalogue of everyday scents, their active ingredients and current production methods, as a starting point for teams looking for compounds worth making sustainably. Six cym operon genes were submitted to the Registry as basic parts (BBa_26CFFF0H, BBa_26R7VUFV, BBa_26MJ8EI9, BBa_26SS8791, BBa_26AS8UG2, BBa_26AW7YAF).

images.caption: NetFlux architecture: React/TypeScript frontend, FastAPI backend with Pydantic schemas and a bounded JobManager worker pool, over a SQLite model catalogue and precomputed Mass Flow Graphs.
The five-stage NetFlux pipeline: Mass Flow Graph construction, FASTCC pruning, SCOPE/GUDIE corridor extraction, FVA annotation, and the pooled OptKnock/OptForce design engine.
An extracted production corridor drawn automatically from a genome-scale model, flowing left to right with line width proportional to mass flow and reactions coloured by FVA annotation.
The intervention strategy suite: ranked designs with yield floor, retained growth, coupling strength and the specific gene to edit, separated from weaker exploratory leads.

gemsTakeaway: When there is no ground truth to benchmark against, define what a correct output must satisfy and measure that: NetFlux's credibility rests on three published numbers (100% corridor connectivity, 7.8% of the network retained, 0.863 recall of independently FVA-derived essential reactions), with the weakest organisms named. A research centre should also copy the ephemeral-compute design, user-uploaded models held in RAM behind short-lived tokens and never written to disk, which makes a shared analysis service usable with data people will not hand over.
